inspiration: Screen stack for the whole client: lineage.js holds a list of controllers (login, character select, game) with a push that renders the new screen and a current() accessor. Keep the idea: one stack drives login, character select, world and any menu. Defect: pop() on line 22 returns slice(index, 0), which returns an empty list and removes nothing. Fix: remove the controller from the list (splice) and return it. Decision: adapt (idea) with the fix.

Fixed-centre follow view: camera.js positions the character at the screen centre plus the tile offset times 32 px (line 18). The camera move() is an empty stub (line 15), so the world moves only by offset. Idea for the fight camera (parity row 11): keep the hero fixed at centre and move the world by offset; add smoothing and a fight framing that the stub does not have.

One tile unit in one place: the tile component receives tileSize 32 with the renderer size (game_controller.js line 22). Idea: one grid constant passed to every component so the tile, the hero offset and the camera agree.

Components on one stage: the game controller builds chat, tiles, characters and camera as components on one display stage (game_controller.js, from line 17). Keep this split: state in controllers, drawing in components. Good match for the client-only camera/HUD ruling.

Chat as channel tabs with history per tab: engine/chat.js finds a tab list, marks the global tab active and keeps a history array per channel tab (lines 9-10). Idea for hud-ui chat: per-channel history and a default channel.

Small fixed-field movement record: the move message carries a character id, x, y and a one-byte heading (move.js, lines 14-19). Idea for the many-on-one sync (row 18 and post-K item 3): one short record per moving actor with heading, not a full state dump.

briefs.label: Fixed-centre follow view (own label)
briefs.why: The hero stays put and the world slides under it; the motion reads as movement without a moving camera rig.
briefs.keep: hero fixed at screen centre; world offset by tile times a fixed unit; one grid constant shared by all components
briefs.change: add smoothing and a fight framing (wider on the foe, not the hero); no empty move stub; a shake only on heavy hits

briefs.label: Screen stack for login to world (own label)
briefs.why: One stack makes every screen change predictable: push a screen, pop it back, never leave a dead one behind.
briefs.keep: a single controller stack; push renders the new screen; current() is the top
briefs.change: pop must remove (fix the slice defect); our own screens (title, hero pick, fight, pit, results); a fade between screens

briefs.label: Tabbed chat with per-channel history (own label)
briefs.why: Channels keep their own scroll history, so switching a tab never loses a line.
briefs.keep: a global default tab; per-tab history; the active tab state on the tab list
briefs.change: channel names and colour tags of our own; a fight-log channel that is read-only
